A new report published by Counterpoint Research forecasts that consumer wearable devices will generate more than US$1 trillion in cumulative revenue by 2032, with smartwatches and wireless earbuds standing out as the top performers. Here are the category details.

Smartwatches and wireless earbuds are expected to lead the market.

In a report published today, Counterpoint Research stated that "the global consumer wearable device market is projected to generate cumulative revenue exceeding US$1 trillion between 2026 and 2032."

Breaking down the consumer wearable device categories, the report forecasts that hearables will account for the largest revenue share at approximately US$360 billion cumulatively, followed by smartwatches at US$304 billion and smart glasses at US$168 billion.

Excerpts from the report are as follows:

Health patches are projected to generate an additional US$120 billion in revenue, followed by smart rings at US$44 billion, pendant devices at US$24 billion, smart shoes at US$18 billion, and fitness bands at US$14 billion. Smart socks, smart clothing, and smart belts are each expected to generate less than US$10 billion.

Counterpoint Research noted that consumer wearable device revenue is growing at twice the rate of unit shipments, and pointed to what may be an even more revealing phenomenon—the market appears to be shifting gradually from fitness tracking toward preventive health, where "devices can detect anomalies before the user is even aware of them."

As for Apple, the company is already competing in the two highest-revenue categories projected by the report, including AirPods and Apple Watch. Apple is also rumored to be developing smart glasses, while reportedly exploring screenless fitness bands as well as smart rings.

Last month, Apple reported revenue of US$7.88 billion for its Wearables, Home, and Accessories category in the third quarter of fiscal year 2026, representing 6% year-over-year growth and the strongest growth in that category since the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2022.

Although the category covers far more than wearable devices themselves, Apple has been actively expanding this segment for years, and it is evidently viewed as an important revenue source. Counterpoint estimates that AirPods alone will surpass the US$100 billion cumulative revenue mark in 2026.
